brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: Single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n only - 1 piece total, no neighbours at same level or above; get_build confirms 1 piece

Configurator offers max 1 drawer on a half base (cut-face drawer: drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-n) and 0 on a full base. Notch/bay drawers require an empty cell between 2-3 bases beside it - disallowed by 'nothing else beside'. Repeated find_sockets for drawer/notch/bay returned 0. Built 1/5 drawers; 5 in a single base is not placeable.

finish.summary: Built the closest legal build: one North half base with its single cut-face drawer (1 drawer). Five drawers in a single isolated hex base is impossible in Hex Cluster - a half base exposes one cut face for one drawer, a full base offers none, and notch/bay drawers all require additional neighbouring bases/empty cells that would violate 'nothing beside or on top'. Max achievable under the stated constraint is 1 drawer.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
